testbed: ShopLab (custom Flask e-commerce testbed) - vulnerable version
description: Register of the vulnerabilities deliberately introduced into testbed/vulnerable_routes.py and testbed/app.py. The patched version corrects every entry, so its expected register is empty.
matching_rules: A finding matches an entry when the category is equal AND either (a) the URL path and parameter are equal (parameter null = any), or (b) for site-wide misconfigurations, the finding's check id equals the entry's 'check'.

vulnerabilities.description: The search term is concatenated into a LIKE clause of an SQL statement.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: SQLite syntax error (sqlite3.OperationalError) for a quote/parenthesis, and different result sets for TRUE/FALSE conditions.

vulnerabilities.description: The numeric product id is concatenated into the WHERE clause without validation.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: 'unrecognized token' error for a quote; product page for 'id AND 1=1' and not-found page for 'id AND 1=2'.

vulnerabilities.description: The search term is rendered with Markup() (marked safe), bypassing Jinja2 auto-escaping.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: Injected marker tag reflected unencoded in the 'Showing results for' line.

vulnerabilities.description: The cart status message taken from the URL is rendered without encoding.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: Injected marker tag reflected unencoded inside the #cart-status alert.

vulnerabilities.description: The profile-update form has no anti-CSRF token and the endpoint is exempt from token validation.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: POST without a token is accepted (redirect to /profile?msg=Profile updated).

vulnerabilities.description: The checkout / place-order form has no anti-CSRF token and the endpoint is exempt from token validation.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: POST without a token is processed by the order logic instead of being rejected.

vulnerabilities.description: Order details are returned for any order id without checking that the order belongs to the logged-in user.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: User B receives HTTP 200 with user A's order details (customer name, address, items).

vulnerabilities.description: Any logged-in user can view any customer's profile (email, address) by changing user_id.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: User B receives HTTP 200 with user A's profile.

vulnerabilities.description: No security headers are sent on any response.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: Headers absent from all HTML responses.

vulnerabilities.description: SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=False and no SameSite attribute on the Flask session cookie.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: Set-Cookie: session=...; Path=/  (no HttpOnly, no SameSite).

vulnerabilities.description: Unhandled exceptions are shown to the user with exception type, Python version, platform and a full stack trace.
vulnerabilities.expected_evidence: 'Traceback (most recent call last)' and 'sqlite3.OperationalError' in HTTP 500 responses.
